nodes.name: Solvothermal synthesis of WS2 superstructure
nodes.procedure: In a typical experiment, 0.4 mmol WCl₆·×H₂O, 3.6 mmol sulfur powder, 18 ml ethanol, and 10 mL octylamine were mixed thoroughly in 100 mL Teflon-lined autoclave. The mixed solution was warmed to 200 °C and held for 48 h, and then the whole system was gradually cooled to ambient temperature. Finally, the resulting black samples were centrifuged, washed (ethanol), and vacuum dried (60 °C) to obtain the WS₂ superstructure sample. The optimal synthesis conditions for this method were 200 °C and 48 h, and the method has good repeatability and is feasible for scalable preparation.

nodes.characterization_summary: Caterpillar-like 3D nanostructure comprised of staggered and vertically aligned nanosheets with lateral sizes 300-500 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2a, b shows that the obtained samples are caterpillar-like and comprised of staggered and vertically aligned nanosheets with lateral sizes ranging from 300 to 500 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals the WS₂ superstructure morphology. Scale bar, 200 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: b TEM image of the WS₂ superstructure. Scale bar, 200 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM image shows staggered and vertical alignment between layers; EDS mappings show uniform W and S distribution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HAADF-STEM image and the corresponding energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mappings demonstrate the uniform distribution of W and S elements in the sample (Fig. 2c and Supplementary Fig. 4).

nodes.characterization_summary: (002) diffraction peak shifted to 8.9° corresponding to expanded layer spacing of 0.98 nm. Peak at 2θ ≈ 17.6° indicates additional separation of 5.0-5.2 Å. Strongest (002) peak indicates c-axis extended structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 2d, the (002) diffraction peak of the WS₂ superstructure shifted to 8.9° compared with the 1T-WS₂ and 2H·WS₂ samples, corresponding to an expanded layer spacing of 0.98 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: Clear lattice fringes with d-spacings of 0.52 and 0.94 nm observed in stepped edge surface-terminated structure. Crystal fringes along the edge are stepped.
nodes.evidence_snippet: It is worth noting that the crystal fringes along the edge are stepped for the WS₂ superstructure sample (Fig. 2e, f). The clear lattice fringes with d-spacings of 0.52 and 0.94 nm were observed in the stepped edge surface-terminated structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: Hybrid 1T/2H phase: 1T phase W 4f7/2 31.8 eV, W 4f5/2 33.8 eV (82.1%); 2H phase W 4f7/2 32.7 eV, W 4f5/2 34.7 eV (17.9%).
nodes.evidence_snippet: double peaks located at 31.8 eV and 33.8 eV are ascribed to the core levels of W 4f7/2 and W 4f5/2 of 1T phase WS₂ in the sample, respectively. Two peaks of WS₂ superstructure at 32.7 eV (W 4f7/2) and 34.7 eV (W 4f5/2) are the characteristics of W for 2H phase WS₂... The relative ratio of 1T phase and 2H phase occupies 82.1% and 17.9%.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectroscopy confirms hybrid 2H/1T structure identical to XPS results.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Identical conclusion was obtained in the Raman spectroscopy analysis (Supplementary Fig. 7).

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM shows single curved WS₂ superstructure formed by orientation-dependent assembly of nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The AFM image presented in Fig. 3a clearly shows a single curved WS₂ superstructure formed by the orientation-dependent assembly of nanosheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: Surface potential varies with length and curvature; electron enrichment at high strain concentration regions.
nodes.evidence_snippet: KPFM test reveals the surface potential of WS₂ superstructure on the Si substrate (Fig. 3b). As shown in Fig. 3c, the three different positions in the WS₂ superstructure (marked with different symbols) show a clear potential discrepancy, indicating the enrichment of surface electrons at the high strain concentration region.

nodes.characterization_summary: Increased ESR intensity reveals significant unpaired electron enrichment due to electronic rearrangement between W-d and S-p orbitals.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The increased ESR intensity further reveals the characteristics of significant unpaired electron enrichment in WS₂ superstructure crystals due to the electronic rearrangement between W-d and S-p orbitals.

nodes.characterization_summary: Uniform distribution of W and S elements confirmed by EDS elemental mappings.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HAADF-STEM image and the corresponding energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mappings demonstrate the uniform distribution of W and S elements in the sample.

nodes.characterization_summary: ECSA calculated as 320.8 cm²_ECSA using double-layer capacitance (Cdl) method.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The ECSA value of WS₂ superstructure is 320.8 cm_ECSA², which is significantly larger than that of 1T·WS₂ (239.2 cm_ECSA²) and 2H-WS₂ (13.7 cm_ECSA²).

nodes.characterization_summary: Charge transfer resistance Rct = 3.87 ± 0.03 Ω, indicating superior charge transfer kinetics.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The WS₂ superstructure sample exhibited remarkably lower charge transfer resistance (3.87 ± 0.03 Ω) than the other samples.
